title: [v5.8] packit: don't propose pre-releases to stable
body:
Fedora's policy is that unstable pre-releases shouldn't be pushed to stable. This PR prevents Packit from proposing downstream PRs for release candidates, e.g. `v6.2.0-rc1`, into stable Fedora streams.

Documentation for `upstream_tag_exclude` [here](https://packit.dev/docs/configuration#upstream_tag_exclude).

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
None
```

comments.body:
Please include the branch name in the PR title for backports as it is not visible for maintianers otherwise on the PR list.
Also I recommend first getting the PR https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/30227 landed in main before opening backports in case changes would be requested there.
I mean for the fedora packing stuff we can make exceptions of course but generally each patch must go into main first to ensure it is carried forward in the future and we do not regress again if it never ends up being merged on main.
FWIW there wont be further RC releases on this branch since 5.8 will only get patch releases at this point but it certainly does not harm to keep the configs bits a bit more in sync
